title: Tune API gateway buffering and routing rules to stabilize streaming and OpenAI compatibility
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: customers reported intermittent truncated streams and tool-calling delivery anomalies when payloads were near gateway limits. The OpenAI compatibility layer exposed differences in how our proxy buffered and chunked responses vs upstream behavior which caused some SDKs to treat tool/function events as complete early. This change makes three pragmatic tweaks: 1) increase streaming proxy soft buffer and add backpressure heuristics to reduce partial flushes on bursty token production; 2) introduce a lightweight routing rule that sends requests with payload+prompt size > 32KB to the throughput pool instead of the low-latency pool; 3) make the OpenAI compatibility layer explicit about 413/429 semantics and stable chunk boundaries for structured output and function-calling events.

What changed (high level):
- Streaming proxy: default soft buffer increased from 16KB -> 48KB, with adaptive flush thresholds based on observed downstream ACK latency. Added a per-connection backpressure counter that delays non-essential 0-byte flushes for 250ms when burstiness detected.
- Routing: new routing heuristic in gateway/router that computes request_size = prompt_bytes + serialized_tool_inputs. If request_size > 32KB, route to pool:throughput-v2. If <= 32KB, route to pool:lowlatency-v1. This is opt-in behind a feature flag gateway.routing.size_based (defaults on for main).
- OpenAI compatibility layer: emit 413 Payload Too Large when request_size exceeds gateway.max_payload_bytes (configurable, default 128KB). Ensure streamed events that implement structured output ("event: function_call|structured|message") are always terminated by a zero-length chunk with a special boundary ticket to avoid partial parsing by clients.
- Tests & docs: added new e2e tests simulating bursty token production with deterministic latency injection. Updated streaming.md docs with behavior notes for SDKs and recommended knobs (client-side reconnect, chunk reassembly).

Why these values: compromises between latency and correctness. 48KB soft buffer reduces spurious partial flushes observed in canary while keeping tail latencies within SLO. 32KB routing threshold reflects 95th percentile prompt+tool payload for high-interaction customers without penalizing the typical chat message.

Rollout plan: feature gated and rolled out as: 10% of traffic (03/01), 50% (03/02), 100% (03/04). Monitoring: new metrics gateway.stream.partial_flush_rate and gateway.routing.large_request_ratio added to the console. Canary results: partial_flush_rate dropped ~74% in canary, CPU rose 6% on throughput pools within expected bounds.

Backward compatibility & migration notes: clients relying on previous chunking semantics should be compatible; SDKs that reassemble events by delimiter should accept the explicit zero-length chunk boundary. For customers hitting 413, guidance added: either reduce prompt size or increase dedicated pool limits (via Dedicated config) or contact support to raise gateway.max_payload_bytes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation
- [x] Unit tests for routing decision and proxy buffer
- [x] E2E injection tests simulating bursty token streams
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Metrics & dashboards added
- [x] Rollout schedule and rollback plan

Notes: This PR intentionally does not change default gateway.max_payload_bytes (128KB) — this keeps existing deployments stable while improving streaming behavior. Gateway routing size_based defaults to enabled; if we see any regressions in low-latency percentiles we can toggle the flag and revert routing changes independently.
